# MCP tools

What `tripshots mcp` offers an agent. Long-running tools (`find_footage`, `make_reel`, `render_reel`, `list_trips`, `people_discover`) start a background job, wait a while (about 50 s; `render_reel` 20 s), and otherwise return the job id to poll with `job_status`. See [AI agents](agents.md) for setup.

## Server instructions

Sent to the agent when it connects:

```text
TripShots turns the user's own travel photos and clips into beat-synced Instagram Reels
(1080x1920, or 1920x1080 for a horizontal reel). Nothing is generated: every frame is the user's footage.

Workflow for a request like "a reel about my days in Yellowstone" or "a reel of the photos I'm in":
1. `status` once: footage folders, known people, AI backend. If no footage folders are set, ask the user
   where their footage lives and call `set_footage_folders`.
2. Turn the request into a search: `find_footage` (place / people / dates / kinds). For "me / I / my photos",
   use people=["me"]. If "me" (or a named person) isn't known yet, ask for 2-5 photos of them and call
   `people_add`, or run `people_discover` and ask the user which cluster is them (`people_name`).
   Unsure which trip they mean? `list_trips` shows dates and places.
3. Look at the contact sheet `find_footage` returns. Too few files (< ~8) makes a thin reel: widen the search.
4. `make_reel` with the selection id (dry_run=true first). Pick music from `list_music` or ask; without
   music the reel is silent at 100 BPM. Choose a style from `list_styles` to match the mood.
5. Look at the storyboard image. Fix weak slots with `edit_plan` (swap shots from `shot_candidates`,
   change the hook text: 7 words max, transitions), then `render_reel`.
6. Give the user the mp4 path, cover and caption. Offer one concrete tweak.
Make the creative calls yourself; the user is not a video editor.
```

## status

What TripShots knows: footage folders, music folders, people it can recognise, AI backend, where reels go,
recent jobs. Call this first.

## set_footage_folders

Remember where the user's photos/videos live (searched recursively). Replaces the current list.

| Parameter | Type | Default |
|---|---|---|
| `folders` | array of string | **required** |

## set_folders

Where finished reels are written, and where the user keeps music for reels.

| Parameter | Type | Default |
|---|---|---|
| `reels_folder` | string/null | null |
| `music_folders` | array/null | null |

## manage_reel

A reel as a project: action pin | unpin | favorite | unfavorite | collection (value: a name, or null to take it
out) | rename (value: new name; every file of the reel moves, undo history too) | duplicate (value: optional
name; a copy of the plan to try something else) | delete (moves its files to the Trash; ask the user first).

| Parameter | Type | Default |
|---|---|---|
| `plan` | string | **required** |
| `action` | string | **required** |
| `value` | string/null | null |

## split_trip

One trip in parts (a day each, or a place each: by "day" | "place"), each a saved selection. trip: an id from
list_trips (none = all footage folders). make: cut a reel from every part (plan_only: storyboards first), filed
in the trip's collection. Returns the parts with their selection ids (and plans when made).

| Parameter | Type | Default |
|---|---|---|
| `trip` | string/null | null |
| `by` | string | "day" |
| `make` | boolean | false |
| `plan_only` | boolean | true |
| `style` | string/null | null |
| `music` | string/null | null |

## carousel

A carousel post (1080x1350 slides) from a reel. Without ops: make it (best shots, the hook on the cover, a
route slide last). With ops: change the one made before, e.g. [{"op":"move","from":3,"to":1},
{"op":"layout","slide":2,"layout":"duo"|"trio"|"single"}, {"op":"swap","slide":2,"shot_id":"S040","cell":1},
{"op":"crop","slide":2,"cell":1,"zoom":1.4,"x":0.4,"y":0.5}, {"op":"add","shot_id":"S040","at":3},
{"op":"remove","slide":4}, {"op":"title","text":"..."}, {"op":"handle","text":"name"}, {"op":"route","on":false}].
Returns the slides (files) and checks.

| Parameter | Type | Default |
|---|---|---|
| `plan` | string | **required** |
| `ops` | array/null | null |
| `slides` | integer | 8 |
| `title` | string/null | null |
| `handle` | string/null | null |
| `route` | boolean | true |

## list_effects

The effects library: transitions (for edit_plan transition), text motions (edit_text motion) and text looks
(edit_text style look), and shot effects (edit_plan effect), each with its energy, mood and what it suits.
edit_plan {"op":"auto_effects"} lets the effects director choose for the whole reel.

## list_trips

The user's footage grouped into trips: dates, number of days, places (from GPS), photo/video counts and
per-day places. Use it to resolve "my Iceland trip", "last summer", "the day at the lake".

| Parameter | Type | Default |
|---|---|---|
| `folders` | array/null | null |

## find_footage

Find photos/videos and save them as a selection for make_reel. Returns counts, days, places, people,
a selection id ("sel:xxxx") and a contact sheet to check.

place: a real place name, as specific as helps ("Yellowstone National Park", "Lisbon", "Moraine Lake").
  Matches GPS inside the place's outline, folder/file names, and known place names.
people: who must appear, e.g. ["me"], ["me", "mom"] (any_people=true for either). Faces are recognised on
  this computer; unknown names need people_add / people_name first.
date_from/date_to: YYYY-MM-DD. kinds: both | photo | video.
whole_days: also include same-day files without GPS (phone clips) during the place's hours (default true).
text: words that must appear in the folder/file/place name.
camera: drone | phone | action | camera: only footage from that kind of camera ("all my drone footage" ->
  camera="drone"), told from the camera's make, its file names and what the AI saw in the shots.

| Parameter | Type | Default |
|---|---|---|
| `place` | string/null | null |
| `people` | array/null | null |
| `date_from` | string/null | null |
| `date_to` | string/null | null |
| `near_lat` | number/null | null |
| `near_lon` | number/null | null |
| `radius_km` | number | 10 |
| `kinds` | string | "both" |
| `any_people` | boolean | false |
| `whole_days` | boolean | true |
| `text` | string/null | null |
| `folders` | array/null | null |
| `label` | string/null | null |
| `camera` | string/null | null |

## view_selection

Show a saved selection again: summary, file list (first 60) and a contact sheet.

| Parameter | Type | Default |
|---|---|---|
| `selection` | string | **required** |
| `max_items` | integer | 24 |

## people_list

People TripShots can recognise (name, aliases, number of reference faces).

## people_add

Teach TripShots a person from 2-5 photos where their face is the largest (selfies, portraits).
Use name "me" for the user. Aliases: other names for them ("Abel", "mom" -> "Mary").

| Parameter | Type | Default |
|---|---|---|
| `name` | string | **required** |
| `photos` | array of string | **required** |
| `aliases` | array/null | null |

## people_discover

Group the faces nobody is named for yet into clusters (c1, c2, ...) and return a sheet of example faces.
Show it to the user and ask who is who, then call people_name. First run reads every photo once (slow).

| Parameter | Type | Default |
|---|---|---|
| `folders` | array/null | null |

## people_name

Name a discovered face cluster ("c2" -> "me", "mom", "Alex").

| Parameter | Type | Default |
|---|---|---|
| `cluster_id` | string | **required** |
| `name` | string | **required** |

## list_music

Music the user has: audio files in their music folders and recently used tracks. A reel link
(instagram.com/reel/...) also works as music in make_reel.

## list_styles_and_looks

Edit styles (pace, transitions, text) and colour looks to choose from.

## make_reel

Plan (dry_run=true, default) or plan+render a reel.

sources: selection ids from find_footage ("sel:xxxx") and/or folders/files.
music: an audio file path or an Instagram reel link (its sound is used). None = silent at 100 BPM.
style: from list_styles_and_looks (default: the app's default). duration: seconds (default: the style's).
hook: opening text, 7 words max (default: the AI writes one). location: "Place, Region" label.
captions: subtitles of the words in the music (film dialogue, song lines): auto (dialogue: English, songs: none),
  off, original (as said, in their own script), or a language name/code (english, malayalam, hindi, es...).
no_location: true = no place names on screen at all (no title, none in the hook, no numbered place list).
look: colour look or "auto". route_map: intro | tracker | both | off.
speed_ramps: on | off | which ramps, e.g. "velocity,slam" (velocity, slam, bullet, rush, surge).
speed_up: on | off (fast-forward moving clips in busy sections). drop_speed: rush | impact | both | off.
text_motion: auto | off | rise | focus | tracking | typewriter | slam | write | cinema | decode | stamp: how the words animate
  (HyperFrames; auto picks one per text preset when the runtime is installed).
format: auto | montage | pov | list (numbered places) | series ("Day N of") | reveal. Every reel is planned as a
  story (hook, build, payoff, looping end) and checked by the critic; the result's "score" and "critic" file
  say what it fixed and what is still weak.
recipe: for a style learned from several reels, which reference's recipe (its cut, picture shape and text) to
  follow: auto (the reel whose sound is used, else the one that fits the song), a number (1 = the first
  reference), or off (the style's average).
orientation: auto | vertical | horizontal | 4:3 | 4:5 | 1:1 | sideways (a widescreen edit on its side). auto (default) gives an upright 1080x1920 reel, or a horizontal
  1920x1080 one when the style/recipe is widescreen or the footage only works wide (never black bars);
  horizontal forces a 16:9 file, vertical an upright one (a wide picture then sits in a band).
fresh: on | off. on (default): a series from the same footage doesn't repeat itself: shots that earlier rendered
  reels showed are marked down and their openings and endings aren't reused. off when the user wants the very
  best shots again (e.g. another version of the same reel under a new name).
light: golden | sunset | blue | day | night: only shots in that light (preferred, when too few are).
stabilize: auto | on | off: take the shake out of handheld clips (auto: in calm or held shots).
page: auto | print | route | off: every shot on a page. print = each shot a photographic print on paper (a word
  above, where and when under it); route = each shot in a window over the trip's route map, a pin on where it
  was filmed (shots in the order filmed). auto (default) lets the effects director offer them.
upload_copy: also write a copy without the music (automatic for reel links), so the user can post it and add the
  same sound inside Instagram: do this when the music is a commercial song.
Returns the plan path and the storyboard image to review (or a job id to poll).

| Parameter | Type | Default |
|---|---|---|
| `sources` | array of string | **required** |
| `music` | string/null | null |
| `style` | string/null | null |
| `duration` | number/null | null |
| `hook` | string/null | null |
| `location` | string/null | null |
| `look` | string/null | null |
| `text_preset` | string/null | null |
| `variants` | integer | 1 |
| `route_map` | string/null | null |
| `dry_run` | boolean | true |
| `name` | string/null | null |
| `upload_copy` | boolean | false |
| `speed_ramps` | string/null | null |
| `speed_up` | string/null | null |
| `drop_speed` | string/null | null |
| `format` | string/null | null |
| `text_motion` | string/null | null |
| `no_location` | boolean | false |
| `captions` | string/null | null |
| `recipe` | string/null | null |
| `orientation` | string/null | null |
| `fresh` | string/null | null |
| `light` | string/null | null |
| `stabilize` | string/null | null |
| `page` | string/null | null |

## reel_results

How the user's posted reels did, and what works for their audience. With `reel` (a reel's .mp4 or
.plan.json) and numbers from Instagram Insights (views, avg_watch in seconds, sends = shares, saves...),
records them first. Returns every recorded reel with its score (watch-through and sends per view), `vs_usual`
(its views over the account's median reel: 3+ = a real hit) and the format / hook type that has done best so
far; `make_reel` with format=auto leans on it once confident.

| Parameter | Type | Default |
|---|---|---|
| `reel` | string/null | null |
| `views` | number/null | null |
| `avg_watch` | number/null | null |
| `sends` | number/null | null |
| `saves` | number/null | null |
| `likes` | number/null | null |
| `comments` | number/null | null |

## edit_plan

Change a planned reel without breaking the beat grid. Slots are numbered from 1 as on the storyboard.
edits, applied in order:
  {"op":"swap","segment":3,"shot_id":"S012"}  {"op":"move","from":5,"to":1}  {"op":"exchange","a":2,"b":6}
  {"op":"text","type":"hook"|"location"|"cta","text":"..."}  {"op":"remove_text","type":"location"}
  {"op":"transition","segment":2,"to":"whip"|"zoom_in"|"zoom_out"|"spin"|"flash"|"glitch"|"blur"|"dissolve"|"dip"|"leak"|null}
  {"op":"speed","segment":4,"speed":0.5}  (0.5 slow motion, 2 = twice as fast)
  {"op":"ramp","segment":4,"ramp":"velocity"|"slam"|"bullet"|"rush"|"impact"|"surge"|null,"hit":0.6}
    (hit = seconds into the slot where it slams into slow motion; "points":[[0,1],[0.4,0.3],[1,1]] for a custom curve)
  {"op":"frame","segment":4,"subject_x":0.3}
  {"op":"set","path":"motion.beat_punch","value":0.04}
On-screen text by number (plan_texts lists them):
  {"op":"add_text","text":"Day 3","start":4.0,"duration":2.0,"style":{"color":"#ffd23c","size":110,"position":"upper"}}
  {"op":"edit_text","index":2,"text":"...","start":1.0,"duration":2.5,"style":{"font":"anton"|"gf:Playfair Display:700",
    "size":120,"color":"#ffffff","position":"upper"|"center"|"lower","y":0.3,"x":0.5,"uppercase":true,
    "anim":"pop"|"slide"|"fade"|"scale"|"typewriter"|"tracking"|"rise"|"cut"}}   (null drops a style key)
  {"op":"delete_text","index":2}
Timeline (times snap to frames; later text moves with the cut):
  {"op":"duration","segment":3,"dur":1.6,"snap":"beat"}  {"op":"slip","segment":3,"in":12.4}
  {"op":"split","segment":3,"at":0.8}  {"op":"delete","segment":3}  {"op":"duplicate","segment":3}
  {"op":"trim","segment":3,"side":"left"|"right","by":0.4}  (from the start the clip's end stays put)
  {"op":"freeze","segment":3,"at":0.8,"dur":1.0}  (hold that frame, cut in there)  {"op":"reverse","segment":3,"on":true}
Effects (list_effects): {"op":"effect","segment":3,"id":"glow","amount":0.5} (id null removes)
  {"op":"auto_effects"}  the effects director picks transitions, text motion/looks and shot effects again
  {"op":"page","kind":"print"|"route"|"off","paper":"white"|"cream"|"black","theme":"light"|"dark"}  every shot on a page
  {"op":"page","segment":3,"title":"The Coast","left":"Big Sur","right":"October 2026","label":"..."}  one page's words
  {"op":"log","segment":3|"all","profile":"apple_log"|"dlog"|"slog3"|"vlog"|"flog"|"flog2"|"clog3"|"auto"|null}  flat log footage made normal
Overlay lane and keyframes: {"op":"pip_add","shot_id":"S040","start":3.0,"dur":2.0,"x":0.72,"y":0.28,"scale":0.4}
  {"op":"pip_edit","index":1,"x":0.3,"scale":0.5}  {"op":"pip_delete","index":1}
  {"op":"keyframe","segment":3,"t":0.5,"zoom":1.6,"x":0.4,"y":0.5,"ease":"out"} (zoom onto that point; "remove"/"clear")
  {"op":"insert","after":2,"shot_id":"S040","dur":1.2}  {"op":"music","start":12.0,"gain_db":-3,"fade_out":1.2}
Colour: {"op":"grade","look":"teal-orange"|"none"|<list_looks name>,"strength":0.8,"grain":4,"vignette":true}
  {"op":"adjust","segment":3|"all","exposure":0.3,"contrast":1.1,"saturation":1.2,"warmth":0.2,"tint":0,
   "shadows":0.2,"highlights":-0.3,"graded":true}  (one shot's corrections on top of the look; "reset":true clears)
  {"op":"layer","segment":3|"all","region":"sky"|"subject"|"skin"|"greens"|"water"|"ground"|"edges",
   "exposure":-0.3,"contrast":1.1,"saturation":1.1,"warmth":0.1,"tint":0,"hue":-8}  (a correction on part of the
   frame; "on":false turns it off, "remove":true drops it)  {"op":"layers_auto","segment":3|"all"}
Returns the new storyboard. Then render_reel.

| Parameter | Type | Default |
|---|---|---|
| `plan` | string | **required** |
| `edits` | array of object | **required** |

## plan_texts

Every line of on-screen text in a plan, numbered for edit_plan's edit_text / delete_text, with its timing
and its own lettering (font, size, colour, position, animation); also the fonts that can be used.

| Parameter | Type | Default |
|---|---|---|
| `plan` | string | **required** |

## colour_looks

The colour looks a reel can use (make_reel look=..., edit_plan {"op":"grade","look":...}).
action: "list" (every look: built-in cinematic and travel looks, ones measured from reels, imported LUTs, with
what each does), "packs" (free LUT packs that can be fetched, with their licence notes), "fetch" (items = pack ids,
e.g. ["gmic-creative"]), "add" (items = .cube files, HaldCLUT images, folders, zips or links), "remove"
(items = [look name] or pack=...).

| Parameter | Type | Default |
|---|---|---|
| `action` | string | "list" |
| `items` | array/null | null |
| `pack` | string/null | null |

## write_caption

Write the Instagram post for a reel, aimed at reach: a hook first line, search keywords worked into the
caption, one ask (send / save / comment), 3-5 specific hashtags, alt text, a first comment and two other
opening lines. Saves NAME.caption.txt (ready to paste) and NAME.social.json.

| Parameter | Type | Default |
|---|---|---|
| `plan` | string | **required** |
| `tone` | string/null | null |
| `extra` | string/null | null |

## revise_reel

Notes on a finished reel, each pinned to a time: [{"t": 12.3, "text": "too dark here"}, ...]. The AI turns
them into safe plan edits (swap a shot, colour, text, framing, speed...) using a still of the reel at each
note, then the reel is rendered again. Returns a job id; poll job_status. Writes NAME.revise.json (what was
done for each note).

| Parameter | Type | Default |
|---|---|---|
| `plan` | string | **required** |
| `notes` | array of object | **required** |
| `render` | boolean | true |

## post_reel

Post a finished reel through Upload-Post (Instagram, TikTok, YouTube, ...), now or scheduled (`at` like
2026-12-01T18:00, `tz` like Europe/Madrid). A dry run unless send=true: always show the user the dry run and
get their go-ahead before sending. Only reels whose quality checks passed; never the same post twice.

| Parameter | Type | Default |
|---|---|---|
| `video` | string | **required** |
| `platforms` | array of string | **required** |
| `at` | string/null | null |
| `tz` | string/null | null |
| `title` | string/null | null |
| `send` | boolean | false |

## render_reel

Render a (reviewed) plan to the final mp4: video, cover, caption, sound design. Takes a few minutes:
returns a job id; poll job_status.

| Parameter | Type | Default |
|---|---|---|
| `plan` | string | **required** |
| `encoder` | string/null | null |

## check_reel

Quality checks on a rendered reel (they also run after every render): size/fps/codecs, length, loudness
(-14 LUFS, true peak), black / frozen / silent stretches, text inside Instagram's safe area, text big enough
and on screen long enough to read. Returns the report and a contact sheet of 12 frames to look at.

| Parameter | Type | Default |
|---|---|---|
| `video` | string | **required** |

## export_edit

Hand the edit to DaVinci Resolve / Premiere / Final Cut: writes .edl, .otio and .storyboard.md.

| Parameter | Type | Default |
|---|---|---|
| `plan` | string | **required** |

## analyze_footage

Analyse photos and videos on their own, without making a reel: for every file its capture time, place, camera,
trip and people, and for every shot (a photo, or a scene of a video) technical quality (sharpness, exposure,
colours, near-duplicates, camera motion) and an AI description (caption, description, tags, subjects with boxes,
scene, time of day, weather, people, visible text, landmark, aesthetic 1-10, issues). Writes media.jsonl
(schema tripshots.media/1) that reels, collage apps and other tools reuse. Incremental: only new files cost time.
sources: folders, files or sel:<id> (default: the footage folders). cached: export only what's already analysed.

| Parameter | Type | Default |
|---|---|---|
| `sources` | array/null | null |
| `ai` | boolean | true |
| `faces` | boolean | true |
| `places` | boolean | true |
| `cached` | boolean | false |

## search_media

Search an analysis (default: the latest) for photos/shots: text matches captions, descriptions, tags, places
and landmarks; tags/people must all be present; min_aesthetic 1-10; scene e.g. "food", "mountains"; day
YYYY-MM-DD. Returns compact records (full=true for the whole tripshots.media/1 record).

|---|---|---|

| `people` | array/null | null |
| `kind` | string/null | null |

| `full` | boolean | false |

## edits_package

Prepare a planned reel for Instagram's Edits app (Mac): renders the picture with everything only TripShots
can do baked in (grade, motion, transitions, split screens, maps, titles behind the skyline), and writes the
rest separately so it stays editable in Edits: one clip per shot, the texts (with timings, plus PNGs of
TripShots' styling), the sound effects track, the song and a manifest.json. Takes a few minutes: returns a job.

Then either call edits_push, or, if the Edits MCP tools are connected to you as well, assemble it there from
manifest.json: new project in the manifest's width x height (9:16, or 16:9 for a horizontal reel); clips at their starts (or picture.mp4 at 0); each text as Edits text at its
start/duration; sound-effects.wav at 0; the song from Edits' library at music.song_start. Use paths under
'staged' when present (Edits can only open files in its own container). Don't export or post unless asked.

| Parameter | Type | Default |
|---|---|---|
| `plan` | string | **required** |
| `clips` | boolean | true |

## edits_status

Is Edits reachable, which automation tools does it offer, and is TripShots' mapping to them confirmed?

## edits_push

Build the timeline in Edits from an edits_package folder, through the user's confirmed tool mapping.
picture: one video clip instead of one per shot. music: library (leave the song to add from Edits' library,
the default), file (add music.m4a) or none. text_as: text (editable Edits text) or image (TripShots' PNGs).

| Parameter | Type | Default |
|---|---|---|
| `package` | string | **required** |
| `picture` | boolean | false |
| `music` | string | "library" |
| `text_as` | string | "text" |
